quest.title: The Kabukimono's Finale
quest.description: The information you gathered left you with a heavy heart. You decide to return to the Sanctuary of Surasthana and tell Nahida about everything you learned...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1125, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

talks.objective: Return to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Hey! It's them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aqaba, Sawada! You're still here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you still talking about the... "essay"?

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Indeed we are! If you have a moment, we'd love for you to join us once more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We have time. What do you wanna talk to us about?

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: The same topic we discussed last time... obviously.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still looking for more info about Tatarasuna, huh? Hmm, should we join them?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perfect. These two have researched Tatarasuna's past. Let's hear what they have to say.)

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, we haven't made any real progress...

choices.text: The article that you let me read last time was great.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Huh? Oh, uh, of course.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: I presume you'll want to read mine as well? Here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The content has changed. Another effect of tampering with the information in Irminsul.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Balladeer said he'd erase two of his names. If he really succeeded, it must have taken all of his might... But still...)

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Well, what do you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A masterpiece!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey {NICKNAME}, remember how last time Aqaba was saying how he wished they could gather more information about all this? Well, we just got back from Inazuma, so how about we tell them what we learned?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: What did you find out? Something big?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's a long story. Basically, we have some friends in Inazuma, and...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell the two writers what you learned about the Raiden Gokaden and Tatarasuna's history...

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Wow! So many new details... Thank you so much for sharing that with us!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Well, well, so it all comes down to one man's desire for revenge... Huh. You heard this from a member of the Amenoma Clan, you say? Then I guess it must be true.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: *sigh* So there's no ghost story here after all...

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: This new information actually lends further credence to my hypothesis — evidently, swordsmiths were seen as having an incredibly prestigious role in society in those days, to the extent that harming them was conceived of, at least by the perpetrator, as a way of exacting revenge against those in power...

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Yes, yes, okay, point taken. You were right, but that doesn't mean I can't carry on with my novel...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaand they're back at it. These guys are really into this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've got some things to take care of. Bye for now.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Oh, so sorry, look at us, prattling on about our projects and ignoring you. Thank you so much for the information.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're welcome. See ya!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Keep us in the loop if you find out anything else!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will do!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, we're here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, how have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ugh, where to start... Paimon hasn't had a moment's rest this whole time. That night, we ended up chatting and chatting until suddenly, the sun was up... And then, {M#he}{F#she} decided {M#he}{F#she} wanted to go to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I was investigating the situation with The Balladeer.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Balladeer... Hmm. Sounds like some kind of code name.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You look troubled... Is there something you need to tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even Nahida doesn't remember... Just like last time, any changes to Irminsul affect her as well.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Balladeer acted quickly. He finished erasing himself before Nahida could stop him...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm the only one who still remembers the things that were erased. Once again... I am the record-keeper.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's wrong...? You look so upset.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are things that have happened... that only I can remember.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have to tell you the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With a heavy heart, you piece back together the story that was broken and scattered across time...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: There once was one named The Balladeer, created by the Electro Archon. He was a puppet who lived among men.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a series of events in Tatarasuna, The Balladeer, thinking he had been thrice betrayed, left Inazuma to roam the world beyond.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With no trust for humans, and only loathing for the gods,\nhe bore his grudge for years as he grew in strength, then returned to Inazuma to take his revenge.\nHe tried in vain to become a deity with a Gnosis, and ended up losing everything.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Finally, he entered Irminsul and learned the truth behind his betrayal.\nKnowing now that his entire life was built on lies, he did the unthinkable in an attempt to reverse his tragic fate...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...That's quite a story.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So this puppet known as The Balladeer erased himself from Irminsul... hoping that he could change the past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how was he even able to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #As {NICKNAME} said, he very nearly became Sumeru's deity. Admittedly, I remember it a little differently... I don't recall finding anyone inside the machine after we defeated it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, it does make sense. If someone were to successfully erase themselves from Irminsul, the world would change to reflect the new reality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you believe this person really existed, and we just don't remember him because... well, because he literally changed the world?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. Theoretically speaking, it is possible to do this, but I'm struggling to imagine the kind of person who would dare go through with it...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} comes from a world beyond Teyvat. That's why there's no information about {M#him}{F#her} in Irminsul, and it also explains why any changes to Irminsul wouldn't affect {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So, if there's anyone in the world capable of retaining memories from a past that has been rewritten, it's you. It's... quite incredible, when you think about it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You can say that again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's having a hard time understanding this Balladeer guy's motivations... Why did he do it?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I can only make inferences based on the information we've been given. As for what kind of person he was... only you remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I... I'm really not sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We were enemies, after all. I don't know his perspective on all this, so I can't say why he did something so extreme...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Did he want to reset everything? Or save someone? Or did he want to completely undo his existence?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("Everything can be set right. It's time to solve this once and for all"... Maybe that's all there is to it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I still remember the question he asked. He asked me, specifically... and my hesitation gave him his answer.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I hesitated because I witnessed Greater Lord Rukkhadevata erase her own existence, but I can't tell Nahida that.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (To put it another way, I know why The Balladeer was so sure it could work... But I can't tell them that.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Something else worrying you? ...Something that you can't share?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...It couldn't change the fate of the ones who had died. Right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Once The Balladeer realized he hadn't been betrayed after all, it must have completely changed his view of the people of Tatarasuna. Now he saw them as friends again.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: He couldn't keep hating humans after that. And if he thought there was a chance he could save his old friends, it would be hard not to try.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...The story makes sense, every part of it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The Balladeer tried to achieve godhood with The Doctor's help. He was unsuccessful, but retained the power to connect with Irminsul.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That power then enabled him to change what was recorded in Irminsul and erase himself, even though he didn't have much strength left.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it does make sense, but... it still ended in tragedy for his friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It just feels so hopeless... He gave everything to do this, but it seems like he got nothing in return.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Yeah. He changed the world in many ways, and yet the dead still didn't get a second chance. Those fated to a tragic end could not be saved.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What exactly did he want to fight back against? The betrayals in his life? Or did he wish he'd never existed at all?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Please wait a moment. I want to check something.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Found it. This should be the one.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #It turns out that... I have a strange way of confirming everything {M#he}{F#she} has told us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: A record from my personal collection. It was tucked away in a corner.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You should take a look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this a fairy tale? Who wrote it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This matches everything I said.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I authored this record myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You... wrote a fairytale that somehow has something to do with The Balladeer?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #When combined with {NICKNAME}'s narrative, it's clear that this story is an allegory. Everything in it is a symbol for something else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, so this record survived from the... past-past?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. Any information about The Balladeer or the kabukimono in other records will have been changed. But I wrote this story in a way that means, it was left intact.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Changing the information in Irminsul changes Teyvat.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But Irminsul can't change information that was well hidden in advance. I guess I must've written this story as a backup before The Balladeer entered Irminsul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's incredible! What a great idea!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #And sending {NICKNAME} into Irminsul with The Balladeer must have been a further precaution. I knew {M#he}{F#she}'d remember everything.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This story is abstract enough that it still resonates with the present information recorded in Irminsul.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #But if we connect all the different pieces together, the true story that emerges is the one {M#he}{F#she} told us... the now-erased life of The Balladeer.

choices.text: He chose such a radical option, and yet...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There once was a lone monster draped in fox fur. The monster found a family of foxes, joined them, and they became friends. The monster lived with the family, day and night, and everyone treated it as one of their own.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Once in a while, the monster would take off its fox fur at night, and lament to itself as it gazed at its reflection in the water: "I am a monstrosity, yet they are too foolish to see it... I pity them."

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But the monster soon found solace when another came to live among the foxes who was not their kin: a kitten, carved from the wood of a white tree, who had been abandoned by the humans.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The kitten, too, wished to become a fox, but its tail was too slender and it could not grow a coat of richly colored fur. Yet when the other foxes saw this, they spoke words of comfort to the kitten: "Even without a tail and fur like ours, you are still one of us."

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Furious at this happy resolution, the monster lit a fire on the mountain. The terrified animals panicked as the fire spread. The only way to extinguish the flames was to make a sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: A gray fox stood up and addressed the monster. It said: "You are the cleverest among us. Surely you can help us find a way to solve this."

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The monster smiled, led the fox toward the fire... and murdered it. The gray fox's heart was turned into a beautiful drop of water, clear, spotless, and pure.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The monster gave the heart of water to the kitten, telling him: "The foxes have decided. You are the one who must be sacrificed. Take this, quench the flames, and die for your fox kin."

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The fire was extinguished, but the kitten lived. It left that side of the mountain and found a little bird who had a broken wing.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The two promised they would spend their whole lives together, but the little bird did not have long left to live. It passed away soon after. After burying the bird, the kitten left the mountain for good.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Never again would it cherish a single creature, nor a single blade of grass that stood on that mountain. The kitten spent the nights wandering aimlessly, gnashing its teeth at the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: How it wished to swallow the moon and devour the moonlight. If the world could only return to darkness, then it would finally be peaceful and content.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: "I will become the new moon, the answer to everything. Then, no one will know that there were once birds, foxes, and cats in this world. And no one can know that they were different."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We solved it!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I remember now. This is not just The Balladeer's story... it is his very own memories. I made a backup so that it would be preserved, no matter what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: To become a god, he was experimented on and modified countless times. It was brutal torture, and the only reason he was able to survive is that he was a puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This memory was extracted from him by the scholars. Presumably, they kept it to have something to defend themselves with...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Creating a deity was just the first step. Some of them wanted to be able to control it. That's why they backed up his memory for later use.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I buried it deep inside one of my own dreams, and then hid it inside an allegorical story so that it wouldn't be altered.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to believe that this person really existed, let alone that he tried to... get rid of us on more than one occasion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has no memory of him at all. He completely vanished, like a puff of smoke...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Balladeer agreed to help me look for information about the Descenders, and although he was unsuccessful, he still helped you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Before he vanished, he confirmed an important detail: that Khaenri'ah was where your twin first came into this world.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...We still don't know how the change to Irminsul will affect the senior ranks of the Fatui, but in all likelihood, they won't even remember their own Harbinger.

choices.text: I've never had this feeling before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like Paimon wouldn't like this guy a whole lot if he was still around. But still, Paimon doesn't like the way it all ended that much better.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This is why wisdom alone cannot answer all our questions. We look, we see, and we comprehend, but the question still troubles us.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So the answer is not everything. People yearn to find the truth and then conquer the troubles they face.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: When you give someone the truth, you give them a chance to choose their own destiny.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To others looking on, this may seem like a pointless endeavor. But for him, the chance to act on his desire to disappear must have meant a lot.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Never forget that even when we walk beneath dark clouds along a road filled with suffering, the light of wisdom is always there, guiding us toward a better destination.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And that is what you have been doing all along.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Nahida's right. Cheer up! How about we go get something to eat? We can pick up this heavy conversation again later!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #Good idea. Paimon, why don't you take {M#him}{F#her} out for a walk to clear {M#his}{F#her} head?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You got it! C'mon, {NICKNAME}, you need to get out of your head for a while. You'll feel much better after taking a walk.

choices.text: ...It feels like life is as insignificant as a feather.

talks.objective: Take a walk around the Grand Bazaar to clear your head

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here~ What should we eat first?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...I have a nagging feeling, like there's something I'm missing. Something important that I'm forgetting...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you gonna answer or what?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, it's just... Give me a minute. I'm still... processing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, whatever you want... Well, Paimon will be right here when you've figured stuff out. Then we can get something to eat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Come on, brain. Let's dig this out... It's gotta be in there somewhere. It was something about Irminsul, and deleting oneself...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Greater Lord Rukkhadevata... forbidden knowledge... Nahida...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? Have you figured it all out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Yes, that was it! Greater Lord Rukkhadevata — she said that no one can erase themselves from existence, not even her.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Otherwise, why would she need to create her own reincarnation in Lesser Lord Kusanali to do the deletion for her? There would be no point.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, why'd you jump up all of a sudden!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...No, I can't tell Paimon. She doesn't know about Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But this is a crucially important detail: It's simply not possible for The Balladeer to completely erase his own existence. In which case, the question is... What happened to him?)
Excuse me, Boss, there seems to be a small problem with the last bill. Look, here...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Hey! Hey, wait...!
Hmm? You mean me?

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: No, not you! That kid! Didn't you see!? Little rascal grabbed my last two fresh Sunsettias and ran off!

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Look. If you're gonna help out here, you can't keep spacing out, okay? What is it, the work's too boring for you? Or has the big city got too many distractions?
...I wasn't paying close enough attention. Sorry, Boss.
I think you're right, maybe it's the city. It's so exciting, it can be hard to focus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's that guy? You know him or something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That guy... is The Balladeer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...He's WHO???

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: You're a strange one, kiddo. You say you don't want any money for helping out here, and then when I actually give you some work to do, you keep letting yourself get distracted...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: I don't want to take advantage, so I'm happy to pay you what I'd pay anyone else, but if you keep acting like this, pretty soon I won't be able to afford to...
No, no, please, I mean it — you don't need to pay me anything. I'm just so thankful you agreed to take on an outsider like me.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: ...You're welcome, I guess, but I got bigger things to worry about. Look — We're all out of Sunsettias. And I promised the lady down the street I'd deliver a fruit bowl this evening.
Leave it to me, I'll find some more. Just a moment, I'll be right back...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: ...Stop.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm gonna level with you, kiddo. I've never met a worker who said they didn't want a wage before, and at first, I got greedy. Couldn't believe my luck... But I figured you'd start asking for something in return eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: You don't want money, you don't take days off, and in your free time all I see you do is wander around, taking in the sights... Are you a... a drifter or something?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That's right. I am.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We can talk more about that later. First, let me get those fruits you needed — Sunsettias, was it? I'll be right back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What do we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's follow him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. Stay out of sight — don't let him see you!

talks.objective: Follow the person you just saw

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, this'll do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though, as you say, he's The Balladeer... What are we planning on doing, stealing his Sunsettias? Isn't that a bit too cruel?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shush.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, alright...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This should be enough. Umm... Ah, guess I should wash them before I take them back...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...If I wasn't seeing this with my own eyes, I would never believe it.)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You two over there, is there something I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! He spotted us!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You've been following me all the way from the city. I'd have to be blind not to notice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You're right, we were following you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Uh, have we met before?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No, we haven't met... But you know me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...I have no recollection...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's complicated, but I do know you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, are you absolutely sure?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I can't just take your word for it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can prove it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You're a puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A puppet? What makes you think that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? You were right! The look on his face...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I guess you do know me after all. That is not something I share with a lot of people...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Look, I'm just a wanderer. But seeing as you've gone to all this trouble to track me down, I'm sure whatever it is must be important.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's somewhere I want to take you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Okay, but please let me deliver these goods to my boss first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you really working for that guy? He said that you don't want any Mora for it. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Yes. I ran into him out in the wilderness during a storm, and he let me take shelter in his cart. In return, I said I'd be his helper for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's oddly nice of you...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Let me take these back, then I'll come with you. Okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, let's return to the city.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Here you go, Boss. I'll leave them right here.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Oh, you really went pick some more... Hmm? Who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Something's come up, and they need to borrow me. Sorry, Boss, I'm afraid I'll be away from the stall for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: ... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: I was just about to pay you anyway. Go wherever you want, kid. Don't waste your time here.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: I get it, okay? You just wanted to help me out to thank me for giving you shelter from the rain that day. Even then, I don't understand why you're so adamant that you don't want any pay for it...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: But look, it was pouring down, and there you were, sauntering along without a care in the world. Like you had nowhere to be, and didn't even care that it was raining...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Imagine you were me for a second. It's a little weird, right? Why's this guy traveling during a rainstorm if he's not trying to get somewhere? And why's he taking a shortcut through the open country if he's not even in a hurry?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: But anyway, taking you in didn't put me out even slightly. You don't owe me a thing for it, certainly not all this... Your time is valuable, y'know? You should go live your life.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...But, I don't...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...No. You're right.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Then I suppose this is where we say goodbye. Thank you again for taking me into the city.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Don't mention it, kiddo. I've run into all kinds of characters over the years... I just hope you find your path.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Alright, done. Thanks for waiting for me. We can go now.

talks.objective: Return to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This looks like Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Right now, you're in a dream I created using information extracted from your memories.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: These memories will show you the raw truth, but be aware that enemies may react just like in the real world. Please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like an immersive experience. It's a good thing we came along...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...You don't need to do this for me. I don't deserve your protection.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We never give up halfway. Well, we had to once... But that was your doing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And now we're just finishing the job.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Alright, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wanderer, this is the Shakkei Pavilion. In your Balladeer incarnation, this is where the Electro Archon placed you after your creation. You had a great many memories here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that because this is kind of like his birthplace?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You could say that, in a sense... You'll see why shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...I hear footsteps.

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: This place is huge... I can't believe the landslide didn't fill it in. I wonder who built it? The Crystal Marrow miners?

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: ...No, there's no way. Look at this exquisite construction work, and so well-preserved, too... No mining crew would be capable of this.

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? There's someone passed out on the ground...
...Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: Y—You're awake!? What happened? How'd you get stuck here? Are you injured?

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: Huh, not a scratch... and these fine clothes... Who are you...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This man is Katsuragi, deputy to Torachiyo's adopted son, Mikoshi Nagamasa. He found The Balladeer in Shakkei Pavilion and took him back to Tatarasuna.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And the rest is history... Well, it used to be...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In the original version of events, Katsuragi was ultimately killed by Nagamasa.

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: Let me get you out of here. Our people are nearby. Hang in there!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: During the Tatarasuna incident, Niwa was murdered by The Doctor, disguised as a mechanic. The Balladeer, then known as the kabukimono, disappeared not long after.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As the second-in-command at Tatarasuna, responsibility for what had happened fell to Mikoshi Nagamasa.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But Katsuragi had sworn lifelong loyalty to Nagamasa after the latter had once saved his life. At Katsuragi's insistence, Nagamasa killed him to put an end to the Tatarasuna incident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida! Nahida!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you...?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Hello, I do apologize for the sudden intrusion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found this guy in the street, but he doesn't seem to remember anything... So yeah, quite an eventful walk!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Lesser Lord Kusanali what happened in the Grand Bazaar...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You say that you are trekking across Teyvat to train yourself... Many other Inazumans who describe themselves in this way call themselves "shugenja." Why do you refer to yourself as a "wanderer"?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Well, it seems more relevant in my case... To me, it sounds like a plant with no roots.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But these two claim that they know me, and that I have a hidden past unknown even to myself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I wouldn't call it the "past," but rather... Uh, this is a difficult one to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I don't like to rely on using terms like this often, but in your case it seems that it ought to be called a "previous incarnation."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, like a past life or something?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. Something far more distant than the past. So far away that you cannot perceive it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Okay, I have to ask... what was I like in my previous incarnation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ummm...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Oh, okay, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You want to tell me, but you can't bring yourselves to say it. Looks like I didn't have the most wonderful existence in my previous incarnation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're just trying to think where to start...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If it's that difficult to talk about, I have no doubt it will be just as difficult to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But I'll be able to handle it. Please, tell me the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Is truth something you care a lot about?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Then I'll be straight with you. In your previous incarnation, you did many things that would be considered evil.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You nearly died because of what other people did... and many died because of you. As a non-human being, you hated gods and humans alike.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You drifted from place to place, never able to settle, even where you found status and identity. You adamantly believed that you were missing a heart.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Actions rooted in persistence sometimes bear bitter fruit. Sometimes, you have to let parts of yourself go, or you'll never be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nahida tells the Wanderer about his past...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I gave everything I had, but it barely changed history at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In terms of the outcome alone... that's true.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...I don't think I can judge everything I've heard purely in terms of right and wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Each choice a person makes belongs to a specific place and time, a chain of cause and effect... a cycle of karma and consequence.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That is the nature of truth. If one thing is right, its opposite must be wrong, and yet dichotomies like this are not enough to explain the world in all of its complexity.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Seems like my previous incarnation wasn't the most likable individual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haha... we're not trying to hurt your feelings, or anything... But yeah, we weren't your biggest fans.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We were each other's enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If we were enemies, why are you trying to help me find the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah, this is so frustrating! This guy's supposed to be our arch-enemy, but now he's just some random stranger we met on the street!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's got so much to answer for, but we can't make him talk because he doesn't remember anything... Ugh, what a weird situation...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali. As the God of Wisdom, I trust that everything you told me must be true?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, it's all true. I can even show you the memories themselves, if you're willing.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Please. I want to see them for myself. I want to experience my own transgressions.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Even though it will cause your present self great mental anguish?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm just a puppet, with no heart and no name. There is nothing in this world for me to cling to, to fill the void within me... except maybe these sins that can never be undone.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Very well. As you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, shouldn't we go with him!? This one's kind of on us for bringing him here...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Whatever danger I might face, it's my burden to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, could I ask you to supervise him on my behalf?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good point, given your, um... unique situation, w—we'd better keep an eye on you!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you. Now, prepare yourselves, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...That was a good batch of Sunsettias, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are we doing back here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hear voices!

dialogues.speaker: Child
dialogues.text: Whoa... This is where you were born? It's pretty! But there's nobody here... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: I was abandoned, like you. I lived here for a while at first, but... There's nothing for us here. We can't stay...

dialogues.speaker: Child
dialogues.text: ...Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Child
dialogues.text: I heard my mom and dad used to make swords, but the factory manager died, and then my dad got sick... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Child
dialogues.text: He kept coughing all the time, just like me. Then, Mom started coughing too...

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: But you can't. You promised me.

dialogues.speaker: Child
dialogues.text: Yep, we're family now. We're gonna be together for ever and ever!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This child didn't have a name. Or rather... The Balladeer didn't know what to call him. His father died before he could name him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After his mother died, the child stayed in their straw hut alone. Some of the neighbors helped to raise him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After leaving Tatarasuna, The Balladeer ran into this child who didn't have a name, just like him. They made a promise to live together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened to the child then?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He died from his illness while he was still very young. The Balladeer came home one day and found that he had stopped breathing.

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: ...Hey! Wh—What's wrong...? Say something!!!

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: ...You promised me we could be family! You're no different from Niwa and all the others... You betrayed me too. Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The voices have gone. It looks like the memory ends here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Great, I can finally move forward with my novel! But what a sad story...

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: I don't know what I was expecting, but... I never would have guessed this...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This place is dark.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Paimon knows this place... It's the Delusion Factory in Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #In the original version of events, {NICKNAME} once encountered The Balladeer here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Such a creepy atmosphere... and so familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I remember this... It was an unsettling place.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look over there!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Well, well, my fair lady, is this run-down factory and these incompetent fools all for me? Wow, you shouldn't have.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Hah. What do you have to gain from belittling your subordinates? You might not want to admit it, but you are a part of this plan.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Perhaps you find fighting in the Abyss to be a more meaningful use of your time? Oh, but of course, even this pales in comparison to being experimented on by The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Heh, what a sharp tongue you have.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Funny how negotiating never seems to be your strong suit. For the task ahead, I suggest you keep your true feelings to yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Hmph, save your breath. I know what I have to do.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I'm sure you think so, but I still think you need to hear it: Don't start thinking you're invincible. And don't let your emotions get in the way.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Surely you're not worried about me?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I just can't have you getting in my way. You and Childe never fail to find ways to complicate things.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: I'm merely lighting a little fire in this chaotic nation, but you... Being tossed out like trash must make you want to destroy it completely.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Do you remember the last time you were here? That was a lot of swordsmiths you killed. I'm sure the descendants of the Raiden Gokaden are still suffering the consequences now.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Look at you... Aw, don't get so sentimental. Now, give that poor little tongue of yours a rest, and stop pretending like you're above everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Bye, then. See you at the victory feast.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ..."Poor little tongue"? Hahaha... She's playing with fire talking to me like that. Who does she think she is?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Forget it. Someone might find me here any minute now. I should prepare to give them a warm welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The plot does not end here. There is more of this story to come. Wanderer, are you able to continue?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Yes, please don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's a few things I'd like to look into. You should go take a walk and try to unwind.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's time to get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've arrived in Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Is that...

dialogues.speaker: Akademiya Researcher
dialogues.text: Considering that Amurta's sage, Naphis, refused to join this project, I'll take part in the experiment in his place.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Welcome. I look forward to a fruitful collaboration.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: When do we start?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You seem impatient? You should know that becoming a god is far from a trivial affair.

dialogues.speaker: Azar
dialogues.text: The biological transformation is a lengthy process. As such, I too would recommend that we commence as soon as possible. In the event that a successful connection is established, his body will become permanently bound to the machine, and he will be unable to move independently of it.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Nothing worse than what I've been through before then, Doctor?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You were the most resilient test subject I ever came across. Thanks to you, I was able to garner a great deal of information.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Alas, after that, you were under orders to remain in the Abyss. We barely saw each other, and it became difficult to further refine the knowledge I had gained.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: That was gracefully worded. Ever wonder what they'd think if they knew that nothing matters to you apart from your crazy experiments?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I suggest you speak to me in a more respectful tone, Scaramouche. The mere fact of your utility does not make you indestructible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...The Doctor again... That was uncomfortable to watch.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That person gives off a very sinister energy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's The Doctor. He's behind all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's normal for him to give you the creeps! He scares the bejeebers out of Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Let's move on.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No matter what lies ahead, I'll face it. Whatever it takes. I'm just sorry that you have to join me for the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You're a god... Do you think I'm evil?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If you accept that he is you, just as you are you, then yes — you are evil.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: In your eyes, are there any differences between humans and puppets?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Do you think there are any differences between your present self and your previous and future incarnations? If not, then what are the differences between humans and puppets?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Whoever has tasted the joys and sorrows of life in the human realm is human. Whoever has loved and lost, cried with grief, howled with rage at the tragedy of death that eclipses the miracle of life... they are human, too.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've seen enough of my past. If possible, I'd like to reclaim the sins that are mine to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No matter the consequences, I won't run from blame or punishment. Whatever I am due, let it come to pass.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Can you return my memories to me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But won't that mean you'll lose your current identity?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've always believed that human lives follow a set of rules, with each person being a collection of past experiences.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: As a puppet living in the human world, my life is subject to the same rules.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Regaining your memories means reverting completely to your previous incarnation. All the emotions that you discarded will return to you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Are you sure you want to do this?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've lived with a void in my chest my whole life. My creator didn't need me, and ever since I awoke, I've just drifted from one place to the next.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But then I met you, and I finally realized that reclaiming my missing sins might be my one opportunity to become my true self.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Is this the true meaning of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's words? A person can't erase themselves, and even though the original Balladeer has gone, this person will live on in his place...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Are a person's sins an inescapable part of their destiny too?)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've always felt I have an innate tendency to yearn for something more, in a way that goes deeper than for most people... But for all my soul-searching as a shugenja, I've never fully understood it. Looking at it now, it seems that I brought this curse upon myself.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So I beg you... grant me this opportunity to gain a purpose. To change my destiny and end my wandering.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Since your mind is made up, I will return to you that which is yours.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Imbecile! Get out of my sight!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...It disappeared... Did we win?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What did you expect? I'd never lose to that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehh, there's that tone of voice again. You're definitely back to your old self...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but it was you inside that thing, too. What have you got to be smug about?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm harsh on myself and everyone else. Just the way I am.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Haha, you sound like you're concerned about me.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: But don't worry. Thanks to you, even if I didn't change a thing... at least I now know the truth.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The memory recovery seems to have been a success. This dream has served its purpose.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Come on. Let's continue this outside.

choices.text: The past will catch up with you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: (...Time to face the music.)

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: (I'd better make some notes and then get working on my essay.)

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: (Asking the Traveler to help out was definitely the right call.)

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: (Just an honest guy doing some honest business!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go get a snack from one of the stalls in the Grand Bazaar. That'll be sure to lift our spirits!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It must be really tough being the only one who remembers all that... But Paimon's always here to help cheer you up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Katsuragi seems like he was a good guy.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He looks like a warrior, but he has a kind face.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Why couldn't he live a long and happy life?

dialogues.speaker: Katsuragi
dialogues.text: Nagamasa, I found this young guy in a cave sealed off by a landslide. He doesn't remember his name.

dialogues.speaker: Mikoshi Nagamasa
dialogues.text: ...Well, we need to call you something. I hear the workers are calling you "the kabukimono"?

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: That's fine with me.

dialogues.speaker: Mikoshi Nagamasa
dialogues.text: Katsuragi, report to Niwa. Tell him we have someone new joining us.

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: You do realize you're blocking my path?

dialogues.speaker: The Jester
dialogues.text: I come not to obstruct you. I have been waiting.

dialogues.speaker: The Jester
dialogues.text: What you are, truly, is a weapon, one that could be wielded with an iron will... or, you could continue to drift aimlessly.

dialogues.speaker: Kabukimono
dialogues.text: ...Are you trying to win me over?

dialogues.speaker: The Jester
dialogues.text: The long-fated rebellion has begun. Why not take your place at the banquet and join those who shall feast?

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Why are you staring at me in silence? Can't you think of a nicer way to express yourself?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I'm under no obligation to be nice to you. Besides, I thought nothing mattered to you except results and your own interests. Isn't that right... witch?

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Hehe... Muddle-headed puppet, you're only No. 6 because you can take more abuse than other humans. Do you really count that as an asset?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: You're about as much fun to be around as a raging inferno. But before we murder each other, it'd be best if we finish our duties.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...This is trying my patience.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you got all your memories back now?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Have you got any more stupid questions!?
